title: Optimize Suggestion Safety Gate: staged application, automated rollback, and decision hooks
creator: Aria Chen
description: Implement a safety-gated autonomous apply flow for Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching/caching/quantization profiles) that enables low-touch adoption while preventing regressions. The flow must support staged canaries, explicit approval hooks for high-risk changes, automated rollback triggers, audit logging, and developer/ops controls (TTL, percent ramp, metrics windows).
acceptance_criteria: Engine can schedule an Optimize suggestion as a gated rollout object with configurable stages: initial canary percentage, ramp steps, and hold durations
Canary stage metrics evaluated automatically against baseline: token cost delta, median/95p latency, error rate; thresholds configurable per suggestion type
Automated rollback applies when any configured threshold is exceeded during a stage; rollback is recorded in audit log and a notification is sent to on-call and suggestion owner
Approval hooks available: suggestions tagged high-risk require explicit approver action before progressing beyond canary
Console UI surfaces per-stage metrics, progress, and provides manual override (pause/abort/force-apply), and all actions generate immutable audit entries
End-to-end e2e test coverage for staging, rollback triggers, and approval flows in the Optimize integration tests
implementation_notes: Introduce a 'rollout' CRD in the Optimize control plane to represent staged applies (metadata: suggestion_id, owner, policy, stages)
A separate enforcement worker evaluates metrics windows and decides stage progression or rollback; use existing metric aggregation infra (console dashboards / metrics-api)
Default safe thresholds: latency increase > 20% OR error rate increase > 1% OR cost increase > 3% => trigger rollback; make defaults configurable per tenant
Use incremental traffic shifts: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with hold windows (default 15m) – configurable
Approval flow: integrate with SSO identities and RBAC; suggestions flagged by the policy engine as 'high risk' must call the approval API before >20% ramp
Audit trail: write immutable events to customer audit store and internal event log for post-mortem; include pre/post config snapshots
Fallback variants: when a suggested optimization is unavailable for a model or region, route to compatible variant or skip stage rather than applying unsafe config
risks_and_tradeoffs: More conservative defaults reduce cost savings velocity; too-aggressive defaults increase rollback frequency and pager noise
Complexity of per-tenant thresholds and windows increases maintenance burden; start with global defaults and allow overrides per customer
Tight coupling with metrics pipeline means rollout decisions are only as good as telemetry fidelity; plan for graceful degradation (pause and require manual review) if metrics are stale
On-call fatigue risk if rollback triggers are noisy; provide grouping and deduplication of notifications and a cooldown window
